title: It’s a Wonderful Life - A Live Radio Play on Broadway #itsawonderfull...
transcript: As much as I was prepared to be a complete scrooge over this cash grab of a production, I have to admit that it exceeded my expectations. Akin to a concert production of a musical, this feels like a group of all-stars coming together over some low-stakes material to do their thing. The pre-existing IP makes the show inherently marketable, but with such a pared down production, I'd say the cast is the main draw here. No one would claim that It's a Wonderful Life is exactly what Broadway has been missing, nor would someone call this the most inspired holiday production Broadway has ever seen. With plenty of tickets hitting a triple digit price point, it's crazy that such a strong cast is working with such bland material. Performing with scripts in hand, everyone showcasing a fraction of their range, with Megan Hilty the most underused. Andrew Rannells, at least, throws in some physical comedy, but he's also given the most to do. Tituss Burgess steals the show, which I hardly found surprising. All that said, I did have a good time and the production does what it sets out to do. The cast delivers even on a tight leash, and the story is as timeless and saccharine as any good holiday special — it is a classic for a reason. I wouldn't splurge to see this, but it is a perfectly fine production with the right expectations.
reasoning: Creator admits it exceeded low expectations and had a good time, but repeatedly flags bland material, underused cast, and high ticket prices. Lands clearly in mixed territory with the 'wouldn't splurge' caveat.
